A_target.statement:
Let $R$ be a [[Definition:Commutative Ring with Unity|commutative ring with unity]] and $a \in R$.
Then:
:$R \sqbrk x / \ideal {x - a} \cong R$
via $f \mapsto \map f a$.

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi: A \to B$ be a [[Definition:Ring Homomorphism|ring homomorphism]].
Then:
:$A / \map \ker \phi \cong \Img \phi$

derived.the kernel: the principal ideal generated by x - a

object_map.reformulation: Compute the kernel of evaluation by division by the monic polynomial x - a.

validity_conditions: Division by x - a works over any commutative ring because x - a is monic.
Evaluation is surjective because constants evaluate to themselves.
proof_plan: The evaluation map $\operatorname {ev}_a: R \sqbrk x \to R$, $f \mapsto \map f a$, is a ring homomorphism, and is [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] on constants.

By division with remainder by the monic polynomial $x - a$, which is valid over any commutative ring:
:$\map f x = \paren {x - a} \map q x + \map f a$

Hence $\map f a = 0$ {{iff}} $f \in \ideal {x - a}$, so $\map \ker {\operatorname {ev}_a} = \ideal {x - a}$.
This is the [[Factor Theorem]].
